# OpenUI

> Framework-native UI components installed as source. No runtime dependencies.

OpenUI writes components directly into your project for React, Svelte, Astro,
and Vue. Components are plain framework code styled with Tailwind CSS v4; the
`openui` CLI handles configuration, installation, and registry validation.

## Documentation

- [Getting started](https://openui.dev/docs/getting-started): Install OpenUI, initialize a project, and add your first component.
- [Configuration](https://openui.dev/docs/configuration): Every field in openui.json, how discovery works, and how CLI flags interact with the file.
- [CLI](https://openui.dev/docs/cli): Commands, flags, exit codes, and the safety model behind file writes.
- [Components](https://openui.dev/docs/components): The Button API, accessibility behavior, and framework-specific usage.
- [Registry](https://openui.dev/docs/registry): How the OpenUI registry is laid out, generated, served, and validated.
- [Theming](https://openui.dev/docs/theming): Style OpenUI components with Tailwind CSS v4 utilities, dark mode, and local overrides.
- [Contributing](https://openui.dev/docs/contributing): Repository layout, local workflow, verification, changesets, and known beta limitations.

## Frameworks

- [React](https://openui.dev/docs/frameworks/react): Install and use OpenUI components in React, including TypeScript and JavaScript variants.
- [Svelte](https://openui.dev/docs/frameworks/svelte): Install and use OpenUI components in Svelte 5 projects.
- [Astro](https://openui.dev/docs/frameworks/astro): Install and use OpenUI components in Astro projects.
- [Vue](https://openui.dev/docs/frameworks/vue): Install and use OpenUI components in Vue 3 projects.

## Machine-readable

- [Full documentation](https://openui.dev/llms-full.txt): Every page in one file.
- [JSON Schema](https://openui.dev/schema.json): Schema for `openui.json`.
- [Registry index](https://openui.dev/registry/index.json): Components and item locations.

## Optional

- [Contributing](https://openui.dev/docs/contributing): Repository workflow and beta limitations.
